subject: AWS Marketplace SKU descriptions + co-sell next steps
messages:
From: Adam Gibbons <adam.gibbons@amazon.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace: SKU info + co-sell next steps

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the call earlier — AWS Marketplace PM looped me in to get the SKU-level descriptions and any co-sell materials so we can finish the offer page and start the co-sell enablement intake. To move to Partner-Led (co-sell) review we need the following from your side:

- SKU list with 1-sentence purpose and 2–3 key bullets (pricing guidance optional)
- 1-page product summary for the marketplace product page
- Marketing assets: logo (SVG), 2 product screenshots (PNG), and a brief customer use-case blurb
- Confirmation of which SKUs you want AWS to actively co-sell (this affects outreach and enablement)
- Signed co-sell addendum (DocuSign link will work)

What timeline can you commit to for an initial set of SKUs and one-pager? If you can get drafts this week, I can push the offer into final review on our end next Tuesday.

Thanks — looking forward to shipping this.

Best,
Adam
AWS Marketplace Partner Mgmt
[adam.gibbons@amazon.com]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Adam Gibbons <adam.gibbons@amazon.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: SKU info + co-sell next steps

Adam — thanks, sending initial drafts attached.

Attached: redwood_aws_skus_v1.docx (SKU table + short bullets), marketplace_product_one-pager.pdf, brightretail_logo.svg

Quick notes / asks:
- We started with 3 SKUs: "Redwood Hosted", "Redwood Dedicated", and "Redwood Private (VPC)". Each SKU has a 1-line purpose and 3 product bullets. Pricing left as ranges for now.
- Proposed co-sell candidates: Hosted + Dedicated. Private tends to be procurement-led so we didn’t flag it for active co-sell.
- Vanessa / Marcus / Laura — please review the SKU copy and the one-pager for marketplace tone (concise, benefits-first). I flagged a few uncertain phrases in the doc.
- Bright Retail (Sara) is our pilot customer for the marketplace listing; they will provide a 2-sentence use case and logo. Sara — copying you so you can confirm timelines for assets.

Timeline: if internal feedback is returned by end of day Friday (7/17) I can upload to Seller Central and share the draft offer link for AWS review early next week.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Marketplace GTM, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: marketplace_product_one-pager.pdf (one-pager)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Adam Gibbons <adam.gibbons@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace SKU content - suggested edits

Hi team — quick pass on the SKU doc and one-pager. High level: copy is solid, we need to tighten benefit statements and avoid product-sentences that read like internal engineering notes. Specific suggestions below (I used inline comments in redwood_aws_skus_v1.docx).

Suggested edits (high level):
- SKU names: change "Redwood Hosted" -> "Redwood Hosted API" to be explicit on the marketplace page.
- Benefit bullets: start with quantifiable outcomes where possible (e.g., "<50 ms median inference latency via hosted API"). If we can't publish numbers, use comparator language: "enterprise-grade latency for conversational apps".
- Pricing: switch to an illustrative example line rather than ranges; AWS prefers a short pricing blurb on the marketplace page and a link to detailed pricing.
- One-pager: move the customer use case above the feature list — marketplace shoppers want outcomes first.

Also attaching marketplace_activation_checklist.xlsx — this contains items AWS will ask during the co-sell intake (security evidence, compliance statements, Go-to-Market owner). Laura / Marcus — can you confirm who owns the enablement playbook and who will be point for sales training? We should also decide if we want AWS to run a joint webinar as part of the co-sell launch.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Partner GTM
[Attachment: marketplace_activation_checklist.xlsx]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Adam Gibbons <adam.gibbons@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace SKU content - final ok for Seller Central upload?

Nice work — thanks, Vanessa and Hannah. I reviewed the inline comments. Approve subject to two small items:

1) Update the Hosted SKU bullets to lead with performance and security (compliance call outs)
2) Add a short line under "What it replaces" that clarifies typical integration time ("integrates in under 1 week for basic flows") — helps procurement.

Hannah — please make those two edits and then proceed to upload to Seller Central. After upload, please:
- Share the Seller Central draft link (public preview) so Adam and I can confirm display.
- Complete the DocuSign co-sell addendum (I clicked the link Adam shared and it points at the standard AWS co-sell form; I’ll sign once Bright Retail signs).

Laura — re: enablement playbook, we can draft a 30-minute technical demo + 15-minute sales positioning doc; Vanessa will own the webinar ask.

If that timeline works, we can aim to kick co-sell enablement the week of 7/27.

Marcus Lin
VP, Sales Ops
[Attachment referenced: DocuSign co-sell addendum link]

— Sara Lopez
